about.title: Gilroy Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Gilroy's economy runs on a blend of agriculture, food processing, distribution centers, and retail, and each of these jobs carries its own injury risks — from equipment accidents to repetitive strain to falls on uneven ground. In most cases, California law routes workplace injuries through the workers' compensation system rather than a lawsuit against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. But that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim against that third party outside the workers' comp system. Sorting out which path applies to your situation can be confusing, especially while you're recovering. We provide a free case review for injured workers in Gilroy, helping you understand the details and explain what options might be available. There's no cost to find out where you stand.

items.title: Understanding Your Reporting Window
items.desc: California requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim. We can help make sure the right steps are taken early.

items.title: Spotting Third-Party Liability
items.desc: Workers' comp usually blocks a lawsuit against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker may still be liable separately. We can evaluate whether your case involves a party outside the comp system.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you're worried about your job status, we can explain your rights and the protections in place.

items.question: I was hurt while working near Monterey Highway during a delivery run. Can I still file a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: Yes, most on-the-job injuries in Gilroy — including those that happen while driving for work along routes like Monterey Highway or US-101 — are generally covered by workers' compensation regardless of fault. If another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate claim against them outside the workers' comp system. We can help sort out which path applies.

items.question: Can I sue my employer directly for my injury?
items.answer: In most cases, California law makes workers' compensation the exclusive remedy against your employer, meaning you generally can't sue them directly even if they were careless. However, if a third party contributed to your injury, that party may be pursued separately. We can help identify whether a third-party claim exists in your situation.

items.question: What if my employer threatens to fire me for reporting my injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal in California. If you're experiencing pressure or threats after an injury, it's worth speaking with us — we can explain your protections and next steps.
